title: Your Online Financial Advice Just Got Safer: SEBI Chairperson Madhabi Puri Buch's Big Push
description: SEBI Chairperson Madhabi Puri Buch is leading efforts to make online financial advice more trustworthy. The market regulator recently introduced the Common Ad.

faq.a: A finfluencer is a financial influencer, typically a social media creator, who shares financial tips, investment advice, or product recommendations with their audience.

faq.q: Do I need to stop following all finfluencers?
faq.a: No, you don't need to stop following all finfluencers. However, be cautious and always verify the credentials of anyone offering specific investment advice. Prioritise content from SEBI-registered professionals or entities that clearly disclose their registration.

faq.q: How can I identify legitimate financial advice online?
faq.a: Look for clear disclosures of SEBI registration numbers and names. Legitimate advisors or regulated entities will prominently display these details on their profiles and in their content. They will also typically avoid promising guaranteed returns.

faq.q: What if I see misleading financial content or suspect a scam?
faq.a: You can report such content to SEBI through their official channels. SEBI is actively monitoring and taking action against misleading financial information online.

faq.q: Does this apply to all financial products, like insurance or loans?
faq.a: While SEBI primarily regulates the securities market (stocks, mutual funds), the spirit of transparent advertising and avoiding misleading claims extends to other financial products. Other regulators like RBI and IRDAI also have rules for fair practices in their respective domains.
